title: Resource Planning Lead | INTEGRATED RESOURCE PLANNING (IRP)
description:
Job Posting End Date
10-02-2026 Please note the job posting will close on the day before the posting end date.

Job Summary

Are you ready to help shape the future of the electric grid? Join American Electric Power's Integrated Resource Planning (IRP) organization and lead the development of long-term resource strategies that support reliability, affordability, economic development, and the energy transition across multiple states and regulatory jurisdictions.

As a Resource Planning Lead, you will serve as a strategic leader and subject matter expert responsible for managing Integrated Resource Plans (IRPs), evaluating future resource needs, and assessing generation, storage, transmission, demand-side, and emerging technology alternatives. Your work will directly support major investment decisions, regulatory filings, corporate strategy, and long-term planning efforts that impact millions of customers.

This role combines project leadership, quantitative analysis, regulatory engagement, and cross-functional collaboration. You will coordinate teams of analysts and subject matter experts, oversee complex modeling studies, develop planning assumptions, support regulatory proceedings, and provide technical guidance to senior leadership. If you are passionate about energy policy, utility strategy, generation planning, and solving complex challenges facing the power industry, this role offers an opportunity to make a lasting impact.
Job Description

WHAT YOU'LL DO

As a Resource Planning Lead, you will manage the planning activities that support AEP's regulated operating companies and long-term generation portfolio strategy. You will be responsible for coordinating the development of Integrated Resource Plans and related studies while ensuring alignment with corporate objectives, regulatory requirements, and evolving market conditions.
You will lead cross-functional efforts involving commercial operations, regulatory services, load forecasting, environmental planning, generation engineering, transmission planning, and finance to develop and evaluate resource strategies that meet future customer needs.

Key Responsibilities

- Lead development of Integrated Resource Plans (IRPs) and other strategic planning studies across multiple operating companies and regulatory jurisdictions.

- Serve as project manager for complex planning initiatives, coordinating work across analysts, subject matter experts, consultants, and business partners to ensure quality deliverables and adherence to project schedules.

- Lead development of planning assumptions, including load forecasts, commodity prices, technology costs, environmental regulations, transmission constraints, and market rules.

- Direct resource optimization, production cost, and financial modeling efforts used to evaluate capacity needs and alternative resource portfolios.

- Evaluate conventional generation, renewable resources, battery energy storage systems, demand response, energy efficiency programs, market transactions, and emerging technologies.

- Translate technical modeling results into actionable recommendations for executive leadership, operating companies, and regulatory stakeholders.

- Prepare technical reports, presentations, regulatory filings, and expert witness testimony supporting resource planning decisions.

- Respond to discovery requests and provide technical support during regulatory proceedings and stakeholder engagement activities.

- Maintain expertise regarding Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) markets, resource adequacy requirements, transmission planning activities, and policy developments.

- Monitor industry trends, emerging technologies, state and federal policies, and economic development initiatives that may impact future resource needs.

- Build and maintain effective working relationships across operating companies, service corporation departments, regulators, consultants, and external stakeholders.

- Identify opportunities to improve planning methodologies, analytical tools, automation, and business processes.

Technical Skills and Tools

- Resource planning and resource adequacy analysis

- Financial and economic analysis

- Data analytics and visualization

- Project management and stakeholder coordination

- Microsoft Excel, Power BI, PowerPoint, and other business intelligence tools

- Familiarity with Python, VBA, SAS, SQL, or other analytical tools is preferred but not required

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Education : Bachelor's degree in an analytical field such as engineering, mathematics, computer science, or business (e.g. accounting, finance, economics); OR,

Bachelor's degree in a non-analytical field with two years of analytical experience.

Work Experience : Three (3) years as a Resource Planning Analyst Staff; OR,

Ten (10) years of related resource planning experience (in addition to the experience identified above), specifically in generating plant operations or construction, renewable energy, energy efficiency, commercial operations, RTO operations, or transmission engineering/operations.

An advanced degree in an analytical field such as engineering, mathematics, computer science, or business (e.g. accounting, finance, economics) will be considered to be two (2) years of relevant experience.

OTHER REQUIREMENTS: physical demand level is Sedentary.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to explain complex technical concepts to diverse audiences.

- Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional teams and influence decisions without direct authority.

- Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines in a dynamic environment.

- Ability to serve as an expert witness in regulatory proceedings.

- Ability to work occasional evenings and weekends as business needs require.

- Occasional overnight travel may be required.

- Professional certification or licensure (PE, PMP, CFA, CMA, or similar) is preferred.

WHAT YOU'LL GET

In addition to base salary, AEP offers competitive Total Rewards including: discretionary annual incentive, 401(k), pension, health insurance, vacation, educational assistance, etc.

WHO WE ARE

At AEP, we’re more than just an energy company — we’re a team of dedicated professionals committed to delivering safe, reliable, and innovative energy solutions. Guided by our mission to put the customer first, we strive to exceed expectations by listening, responding, and continuously improving the way we serve our communities. If you're passionate about making a meaningful impact and being part of a forward-thinking organization, this is the company for you!

title: NERC Compliance Specialist Lead - Principal
description:
Job Posting End Date
09-24-2026 Please note the job posting will close on the day before the posting end date.

Job Summary

A NERC Compliance Lead ensures that electric utilities, power generators, transmission operators, and related energy organizations comply with mandatory reliability standards established by the North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC). This position will focus primarily on Critical Infrastructure Protection (CIP) standards designed to safeguard the grid from cybersecurity threats. The role is critical to preventing system disturbances, maintaining grid stability, and avoiding regulatory violations and penalties.

In addition, the NERC Compliance Lead plays a proactive role in identifying, assessing, and mitigating compliance risk by reviewing and researching potential self-reports, facilitating self-assessments and audits, conducting research, and serving as a subject matter resource for operations, engineering, IT, and cybersecurity teams. The role requires staying current on evolving NERC standards, industry guidance, and enforcement trends, participating in standards development and ballot processes when applicable, and translating regulatory requirements into practical, executable actions. Through collaboration, education, and continuous improvement, the Lead helps embed a culture of compliance and accountability while supporting the organization’s broader reliability and risk management objectives.
Job Description

What You'll Do:

- Perform interpretations: Conduct research utilizing internal and external resources to interpret the NERC standards as applicable to AEP and provide a written analysis. Lead sessions with business unit partners to discuss the results of the research.

- Oversight reviews: Review all potential violations for reportability determination and to ensure documentation and mitigating activities are accurate, address the root cause, and meet requirements for submittal to the NERC Regional Entities.

- Contribute to the development and maintenance of Compliance Programs: Assist in creating, updating, and implementing policies, procedures, processes, and controls to meet NERC requirements.

- Audits and assessments: Support internal audits, spot-checks, self-certifications, and external regulatory audits. Identify gaps, perform root cause analysis for potential violations, and recommend corrective actions.

- Consultation and training: Provide guidance to business units (operations, engineering, IT, plant staff) on compliance best practices, requirements, and evidence sufficiency. Help communicate regulatory changes.

- Reporting and metrics: Develop compliance reports, dashboards, or metrics. Track status, monitor tasks in compliance tools, and support submissions to NERC or Regional Entities.

- Controls Development and Execution: Contribute to the development, execution, and tracking of internal controls to support compliance risk mitigation strategies. Analyze compliance data, identify non-compliance risks, and contribute to continuous improvement of the compliance program.

- Collaborate: Coordinate cross-departmental efforts, assist with special projects, and support state public utility commission requirements.

What We're Looking For:

NERC Compliance Specialist Lead | Salary Grade 10

Education : Bachelor's degree in engineering (electrical engineering preferred), mathematics, communications, computer science, business, or other related field of study. Advanced degree preferred.
Experience : In addition to any experience required above, eight or more years of progressively responsible positions the in electric utility or similarly regulated industry. Experience in NERC compliance or a similar regulatory compliance is preferred.

Preferred Experience:

- Professional Engineer (PE) desirable

- Electrical Engineering degree preferred

- Certified Power Systems Engineer (PSE) highly desirable

- NERC System Operator Certification

- CISSP, CISA, or other compliance/security certifications

- CRISC or similar risk/compliance certifications

NERC Compliance Specialist Principal | Salary Grade 9

Education: Bachelor's degree in engineering, mathematics, communications, computer science, business, or other related field of study; or an associate's degree in one of the aforementioned fields of study and two (2) years of relevant work experience;
Experience: In addition to any experience required above, seven (7) years of experience in electric utility or similarly regulated industry.
Required: Valid driver’s license

What You'll Get:

At AEP, we’re more than just an energy company!

We’re a team of dedicated professionals committed to delivering safe, reliable, and innovative energy solutions. Guided by our mission to put the customer first, we strive to exceed expectations by listening, responding, and continuously improving the way we serve our communities. If you're passionate about making a meaningful impact and being part of a forward-thinking organization, this is the company for you!

These standards encompass Operations and Planning (O&P) requirements necessary to maintain bulk electric system reliability, as well as Critical Infrastructure Protection (CIP) standards designed to safeguard the grid from cybersecurity threats. The role is critical to preventing system disturbances, maintaining grid stability, and avoiding regulatory violations and penalties.

In addition, the NERC Compliance Lead plays a proactive role in identifying, assessing, and mitigating compliance risk by supporting internal controls, facilitating self assessments and audits, and serving as a subject matter resource for operations, engineering, IT, and cybersecurity teams. The role requires staying current on evolving NERC standards, industry guidance, and enforcement trends, participating in standards development and ballot processes when applicable, and translating regulatory requirements into practical, executable actions. Through collaboration, education, and continuous improvement, the Lead helps embed a culture of compliance and accountability while supporting the organization’s broader reliability and risk management objectives.

- Collaborate on, monitor, and interpret the operational impact of new and revised NERC standards by tracking standards development, regulatory policy activity, and industry trends; actively participate in NERC ballot processes and discussions to identify and mitigate compliance and reliability risks prior to standard approval and translate requirements into organizational applicability.

- Contribute to the development and maintenance of Compliance Programs: Assist in creating, updating, and implementing policies, procedures, processes, and controls to meet NERC requirements.

- Evidence collection and documentation: Gather, review, organize, and maintain compliance evidence (data, logs, reports). Contribute to the preparation and review of Reliability Standard Audit Worksheets (RSAWs), and Audit Readiness Packages.  Audits and assessments: Support internal audits, spot-checks, self-certifications, and external regulatory audits. - Reporting and metrics: Develop compliance reports, dashboards, or metrics. Track status, monitor tasks in compliance tools, and support submissions to NERC or Regional Entities.

- Controls Development and Execution: Contribute to the development, execution, and tracking of internal controls to support compliance risk mitigation strategies. Analyze compliance data, identify non-compliance risks, and contribute to continuous improvement of the compliance program.

- Collaborate with Embedded Support, plant system owners, GEN NERC, and ENRA to ensure that processes are compliant. Coordinate cross-departmental efforts, assist with special projects, and support state public utility commission requirements.

- Work with Operating Company’s Impacted Business Unit Leader (IBUL) to review and approve mitigation plans, RFI responses, and the design of compliance processes and controls.

- Bachelor’s degree in engineering (electrical preferred) Computer, Systems, or Applications engineering, Business, Information Technology, Cybersecurity, or a related field.

- Minimum of four years in compliance, auditing, risk management, power systems operations, or cybersecurity. Prior utility/energy sector or NERC-specific experience is highly preferred.

title: Nuclear GIS Specialist Sr. | NUCLEAR DEVELOPMENT
description:
Job Posting End Date
09-23-2026 Please note the job posting will close on the day before the posting end date.

Job Summary

The Geographical Information System Specialist for Nuclear Siting supports advanced nuclear development by providing geospatial analysis and mapping expertise to identify and evaluate potential sites for nuclear facilities. This role involves managing spatial data, performing suitability analyses, and producing high-quality maps and visualizations to inform siting decisions. The GIS Specialist collaborates with engineering, environmental, and regulatory teams to integrate geospatial insights into feasibility studies and project planning.
Job Description

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Data Management & Analysis

- Collect, organize, and maintain geospatial datasets including land use, environmental constraints, infrastructure, and regulatory boundaries.

- Perform spatial analyses to evaluate site suitability based on technical, environmental, and socio-economic criteria.

- Develop models for proximity analysis (e.g., transmission lines, water sources, transportation access).

Mapping & Visualization

- Create detailed maps, dashboards, and visualizations for internal teams and external stakeholders.

- Prepare GIS layers for integration into feasibility reports and presentations.

Collaboration & Support

- Work closely with siting engineers, environmental specialists, and permitting teams to provide geospatial insights.

- Support interconnection studies by mapping grid infrastructure and analyzing transmission corridors.

Compliance & Standards

- Ensure GIS data and outputs meet industry standards and regulatory requirements.

- Maintain data security and version control for sensitive project information.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree Geography, GIS, Environmental Science, or related field of study dependent upon business unit requirements with three (3) years qualified experience; OR,

- Associate’s degree in the same required disciplines with five (5) years of qualified experience.

- Proficiency in GIS software (ArcGIS, QGIS) and spatial analysis tools.

- Strong analytical and visualization skills; ability to communicate technical findings clearly.

Preferred Skills

- Familiarity with nuclear siting considerations, environmental constraints, and regulatory frameworks.

- Experience with Python or other scripting for GIS automation.

- Knowledge of NRC siting guidelines and NEPA environmental review.

- Understanding of transmission planning and interconnection processes.

WHAT YOU’LL GET

title: Procurement Analyst/Consultant
description:
Job Posting End Date
09-26-2026 Please note the job posting will close on the day before the posting end date.

Job Summary

Are you ready to work in a supportive, fast-moving environment where your work matters? This position supports Procurement Consultants, Procurement Specialists, and Category Managers in the execution of sourcing and contracting initiatives.

In this analytical role, the Procurement Analyst/Consultant supports work including, but not limited to, contract development and administration, contract review and redlining, spend analytics, market complexity assessments, data collection, performance metrics, risk analysis, pricing evaluations, total cost of ownership analyses, demand planning, and reporting. The role assists in evaluating contract terms and conditions, identifying and mitigating contractual and commercial risks, ensuring compliance with company policies and regulatory requirements, and maintaining contract documentation and records.

The Procurement Analyst/Consultant also supports sourcing strategy development, supplier evaluations, and decision-making processes. Responsibilities include coordinating stakeholder reviews, supporting contract negotiations, tracking contractual obligations, facilitating contract execution activities, and providing analytical insights to inform business decisions. The role may lead or direct less complex sourcing and contracting activities while partnering with internal stakeholders, suppliers, Legal, and Risk teams to support successful business outcomes.
Job Description

What You'll Do:

- Conducts market research and analyzes performance metrics to support strategy and decisions regarding suppliers and markets.

- Conducts research and analysis on spend and prior contracts to assist with contract negotiation. Develop and utilize various models (e.g., pricing, total cost ownership).

- Builds and maintains reports to streamline analysis.  Supports bid analysis, as needed.

- Communicates findings and recommendations of research and analysis to Supply Chain, Procurement, and Fleet Operations (SCPFO) and business partners.

- Collaborates, as needed, with the Supply Chain center of excellence (COE), the Service Center, and business partners on projects and other initiatives to address recurring issues, improve efficiency, and improve satisfaction.

- Draft and negotiate contract terms and conditions, analyze commercial sections of proposals and scopes of work, and interface with all disciplines, including legal, risk management, project controls, construction, engineering, finance/accounting and suppliers.

- Prepare, maintain, retrieve and communicate records, reports or documents that may be required to meet corporate and Contract Administration requirements.

- Provide consultative, analytical and contract administration support for commercial operations and senior management.

- Protect the Company’s interest by enforcing warranties and mitigating risk.

- Execute portfolio assignments as requested, perform contract risk assessments, and formulate mitigation strategies.

- Develop Supplier performance criteria and service levels that align with business requirements.

- Manage and oversee amendments to existing agreements using various models.

- Lead the negotiation process through strategy development, issue recognition, and escalation of issues for moderate to complex negotiations.

- Analyze vendor claims and lead in negotiating settlements for a broad range of issues, including impact of changes-in-law and governmental impositions.

- Coordinate, prepare, and track documents to declare, close, and quantify impact of Company force majeure events.

- Ensure all work activities are performed in accordance with the policies, practices, standards, and rules of the company.

- Draft deal summaries for assigned contracts.

- Other duties as assigned.

Education :

- Bachelor's Degree in business, accounting, finance, supply chain, or other related field; OR 4 years of relevant work experience.

Experience:

- In customer service and/or procurement helpful (Procurement Analyst)

Supply chain category management experience, preferably within the utility, manufacturing, or construction industry preferred. (Procurement Consultant)

Preferred Qualifications:

- Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and time management skills desired

- Familiarity with Maximo and Cognos preferred

- Excellent communication skills (written and verbal) desired with an ability to communicate with business partners, stakeholders, and suppliers

- Apply problem-solving skills and use creativity in problem solving.

title: Transmission Planning Modeling Engineer
description:
Job Posting End Date
09-29-2026 Please note the job posting will close on the day before the posting end date.

Job Summary

Job Description Summary

This position is within the East Transmission Planning Modeling organization supporting the PJM region. The role is responsible for the development, maintenance, validation, and quality assurance of transmission system models and associated data used in transmission planning, reliability assessments, operational studies, and NERC compliance activities. The position works closely with internal stakeholders, PJM, neighboring transmission owners, and operations personnel to ensure accurate representation of the transmission system and planned future network changes.
Job Description

What You'll Do:
Based on education, experience, and interview results, this opportunity will be filled commensurately at an appropriate level within the Engineer job family. Minimum requirements are listed at the entry level.
Essential Job Functions

- Develop, maintain, and validate transmission system models used for planning, operational, reliability, and compliance studies utilizing industry modeling tools such as PSS-ODMS and PSS®E.

- Accurately model transmission system topology, impedance, ratings, and configurations for transmission lines, transformers, generators, breakers, and associated equipment across Medium, High, and Extra High Voltage facilities.

- Develop and maintain future network models that incorporate load growth, generation additions and retirements, transmission upgrades, system reconfigurations, and other planned projects while ensuring accurate representation of the as-built system.

- Coordinate with area planning, operations, engineering, project management, and external entities including RTO’s, neighboring transmission owners, and interconnecting entities to obtain, validate, and implement modeling and equipment data.

- Support PJM planning model development processes, including coordination of baseline, near-term, and long-term planning models, PJM submittals, model reviews, and responses to PJM data requests.

- Perform data validation, discrepancy resolution, and model quality reviews using both programmatic and manual techniques to identify errors, inconsistencies, and outdated modeling practices.

- Participate in the planning, organization, and execution of project work activities while managing multiple assignments and deadlines.

- Support compliance with applicable NERC Reliability Standards, including activities related to data quality, model accuracy, evidence retention, and compliance reporting.

- Apply engineering judgment, analytical thinking, and problem-solving skills to resolve technical issues, investigate data anomalies, and develop sustainable solutions.

- Support continuous improvement initiatives through process development, process documentation, implementation of best practices, training, and knowledge transfer activities.

Preferred Qualifications and Experience

- Experience developing, maintaining, validating, and analyzing transmission planning models using PSS-ODMS, Siemens PSS®E, ASPEN OneLiner, TARA, or similar power system analysis tools, including the implementation of equipment data, topology changes, generation interconnections, load modifications, facility ratings, and future transmission projects.

- Experience supporting power flow, short circuit, stability, or reliability assessments using transmission planning models

- Experience modeling transmission lines, transformers, generators, and other electric system equipment.

- Knowledge of inverter-based resources, including solar and wind generation technologies.

- Knowledge of synchronous generation modeling and power system behavior.

- Experience working with PJM planning processes, planning models, or regional transmission organization data exchanges.

- Experience supporting or working with NERC Reliability Standards and compliance programs.

- Demonstrated ability to compare data from multiple sources, evaluate data quality, and perform data correction and clean-up activities.

- Experience developing, improving, documenting, and implementing engineering or business processes.

- Strong communication, organizational, and collaboration skills with the ability to work independently, manage large volumes of technical data, and coordinate effectively with internal and external stakeholders.

title: Sr. SolarWinds Platform Engineer
description:
Job Posting End Date
09-24-2026 Please note the job posting will close on the day before the posting end date.

Job Summary

AEP is seeking an experienced Senior SolarWinds Platform Engineer who is responsible for the design, administration, automation, integration, and support of AEP's enterprise SolarWinds monitoring platform. This role serves as the technical subject matter expert for SolarWinds Network Performance Monitor (NPM), Network Configuration Manager (NCM), Network Insight, network availability monitoring, device lifecycle management, reporting, alerting, and monitoring automation. The engineer will design and maintain enterprise network monitoring solutions across routers, switches, firewalls, VPN infrastructure, telecommunications environments, and critical network services while driving monitoring modernization, operational efficiencies, platform reliability, automation initiatives, and monitoring data quality improvements. The position requires deep technical expertise in network monitoring, SNMP, SolarWinds administration, PowerShell automation, ServiceNow integrations, network device onboarding, reporting development, and enterprise infrastructure operations.
Job Description

What You’ll Do:

Essential Job Functions & Tasks:

SolarWinds Platform Administration:

- Administer and support SolarWinds production, development, and laboratory environments.

- Maintain platform health, performance, availability, and resiliency.

- Perform platform upgrades, patching, maintenance, and lifecycle management.

- Troubleshoot platform-related issues involving polling engines, web servers, databases, monitoring services, and infrastructure dependencies.

- Provide Level 3 support for enterprise SolarWinds monitoring solutions.

Network Monitoring Engineering:

- Design, implement, and maintain monitoring solutions for routers, switches, firewalls, WAN infrastructure, VPN services, and critical network devices.

- Develop monitoring standards, alerting strategies, discovery processes, and onboarding procedures.

- Ensure complete device and interface monitoring coverage across enterprise environments.

- Partner with Network Operations and Engineering teams to improve network visibility and operational readiness.

- Reduce monitoring gaps and improve monitoring effectiveness.

Device Lifecycle Management:

- Manage network device onboarding, validation, updates, and decommissioning activities.

- Maintain accurate monitoring inventories, IP addressing, device classifications, and naming conventions.

- Reconcile SolarWinds inventories with CMDB and authoritative asset sources.

- Support enterprise monitoring remediation and inventory management initiatives.

- Develop standards for onboarding and monitoring governance.

Alerting, Dashboards & Reporting:

- Build and maintain operational dashboards and executive reporting solutions.

- Develop network availability, utilization, performance, and compliance reporting.

- Create automated report generation and distribution processes.

- Design actionable alerts to reduce noise and improve incident response effectiveness.

- Support stakeholder reporting requirements and visibility initiatives.

Service Now and Enterprise Integrations:

- Design and support integration between SolarWinds and ServiceNow.

- Support device onboarding workflows and monitoring request processes.

- Troubleshoot onboarding failures relating to DNS, firewall rules, CMDB data, SNMP communication, and discovery issues.

- Improve end-to-end monitoring automation and operational workflows.

- Support enterprise monitoring modernization initiatives.

Automation & Continuous Improvement:

- Develop PowerShell automation solutions for platform administration.

- Automate device onboarding, inventory updates, interface maintenance, and reporting processes.

- Eliminate manual administrative tasks through repeatable automated workflows.

- Improve operational efficiency through process standardization and automation.

- Drive SolarWinds platform enhancement initiatives.

Platform Architecture & Modernization:

- Participate in architecture, design, and deployment of new SolarWinds environments.

- Define server, database, storage, network, and firewall requirements.

- Support high availability and disaster recovery designs.

- Partner with vendors and architecture teams to implement future-state monitoring solutions.

- Participate in platform roadmap and modernization initiatives.

Production Operations Support:

- Support monitoring platforms providing visibility into critical network services.

- Investigate monitoring failures and implement corrective actions.

- Serve as a technical escalation point for SolarWinds-related incidents.

- Coordinate issue resolution with infrastructure teams, vendors, and operations partners.

- Ensure monitoring platforms align with cybersecurity, change management, and operational standards.

- Protect sensitive infrastructure and monitor data.
